- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (especially > -0.67 change), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After strong upward sentiment spikes (sentiment > 0.67 for 3+ days), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent high.
- If sentiment is flat or mildly negative (avg < 0.33) and news volume is steady, model underestimates downward drift — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a new sentiment cycle — adjust forecast upward by 3–8% for first 3–5 days of a new trend.
- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.67), model often fails to capture lagged momentum — delay forecast peak by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is volatile (large swings > ±0.67) and news volume is high, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
